(Section)
Among these is His saying, exalted is He: ﴿Nun. By the pen and what they inscribe. You are not, by the favour of your Lord, a madman.﴾

The correct view is that nūn, qāf and ṣād are among the letters of the alphabet with which the Lord, glorified is He, opens some of the surahs. They are single, double, triple, quadruple and quintuple letters, and they do not exceed five. Whenever they occur at the beginning of a surah, the Qur'an is mentioned after them, either as something sworn by or as something reported about, with the exception of two surahs, Kaf Ha Ya 'Ayn Sad and Ta Ha, as in His saying: ﴿Alif Lam Mim. This is the Book﴾; ﴿Alif Lam Mim. Allah, there is no god but Him, the Living, the Self-Subsisting. He has sent down upon you the Book﴾; ﴿Alif Lam Mim Sad. A Book has been sent down to you﴾; ﴿Alif Lam Ra. These are the verses of the wise Book﴾; and so on to the end.

In this there is an indication of the nobility and greatness of these letters, since they are the building blocks of His speech and His books, through which He spoke, sent them down upon His messengers, guided His servants, and made Himself, His names, His attributes, His acts, His commands and prohibitions, His threats and promises known to them, and through them made known to them good and evil, the fine and the ugly. He enabled them to speak with them, so that they can convey what is in their souls by the easiest way, with least cost and hardship, and in the most direct and clear manner. This is among the greatest of His blessings upon them, just as it is among the greatest of His signs. For this reason He blamed those who worship a god that does not speak, and He favoured His servants by enabling them to express themselves through these letters by speech. Thus mention of these letters contains an indication of His perfect lordship and His perfect beneficence and bounty. They are therefore more deserving to be sworn by than night and day, the sun and moon, the heaven and the stars, and other created things, for they are the clearest proof of His oneness, His power, His wisdom, His perfection, His speech and the truthfulness of His messengers.

By these letters the Qur'an was taught, by them clear speech was taught, by them man was preferred over the rest of the animal kinds, by them He sent down His books, by them He sent His messengers, by them knowledge was gathered and preserved, by them the interests of His servants in this life and the next were ordered, by them truth is distinguished from falsehood and sound from corrupt, by them scattered sciences were brought together, and by them it became possible to transmit them in minds. How much blessing has been brought by them, how much calamity has been averted by them, how many stumbles have been forgiven by them, how much sanctity has been upheld by them, how much misguidance has been guided by them, how much truth has been established by them and how much falsehood has been demolished by them. Thus His signs in teaching speech are like His signs in the creation of man. Had it not been for the wonders of God's creation, these virtues would not have been established in flesh or sinew. Glory be to Him whose making is such that air emerges from the windpipe, is gathered in the throat, and spreads out in the far back of the mouth, its middle and its end, its top and its bottom, over the middle of the tongue and its edges, between the front teeth, and on the two lips and the nasal passage; so that at each of these articulation points a sound is heard different from the sound of the adjacent point, and it becomes a letter.

Then God inspires man to join some of these together, and they become words standing by themselves. Then He inspires them to compose these words together, and they become speech indicating various meanings: command, prohibition, report, question, negation, affirmation, acknowledgment, denial, confirmation, denial, obligation, recommendation, asking and answering, and other kinds of address, in verse and prose, brief and extended, across the differences of the languages of creatures. All of this is His making, blessed and exalted, in pure air emerging from the inside of man to the outside, through channels prepared and made ready for cutting it, shaping it and then joining and conveying it. So blessed is Allah, Lord of the worlds, the best of creators. This is the state of the created letter.

As for the letter by which created things come to be, its state is higher and more majestic. If this is the state of letters, it is fitting that surahs be opened with them, just as they were opened with the oath, because of the signs of lordship and the proofs of oneness they contain. They indicate His perfect power, His perfect knowledge, His perfect wisdom, His care for His creation, His gentleness and His beneficence. If you give due attention to reasoning from them, you will derive from them proof regarding the origin, the return, creation, command and tawhid, and the message. They are among the clearest proofs of the testimony that there is no god but Allah, that Muhammad is His servant and messenger, and that the Qur'an is the speech of Allah, which He spoke truthfully, sent down upon His messenger as revelation, and conveyed as it was revealed to him, truthfully. Do not neglect reflection on every surah opened with these letters and on how it includes the verses of these matters and affirms them. And success is from Allah.

(Section)
Then He swore by: ﴿The pen and what they inscribe﴾.

He swore by writing and its instrument, the pen, which is one of His signs and the first of His created things, by which His decree and law flowed, by which revelation was written, by which religion was bound, by which the Shariah was established, by which knowledge was preserved, and by which the interests of His servants in this life and the next were upheld. By it kingdoms were firmly established, roads and routes were made secure. It is the most eloquent, most articulate, and most beneficial and sincere orator among people, and a preacher whose admonitions heal hearts of sickness, and a physician who by His permission cures all kinds of pain. It breaks great armies, though it is itself weak and solitary, and mighty men of great strength fear its might and power. By pens regions are managed and kingdoms governed. Knowledge is the tongue of the conscience, communing with it about what is hidden from the ears. It weaves garments of meaning in both directions, so that they become finer than embroidered brocade, and deposits in them its wisdom, so that they become the first flashes of understanding. Pens are the order of understandings. Just as the tongue expresses the heart, so the pen expresses the tongue, and spoken letters are generated by the tongue just as written letters are generated by the pen. The pen expresses the heart, and it is its messenger, its interpreter and its silent tongue.

(Section)
Pens differ in rank. The highest and most honoured in worth is the pen of the prior decree, with which God wrote the destinies of creatures, as in the Sunan of Abu Dawud, from Ubada ibn al-Samit, who said: I heard the Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) say: "The first thing God created was the pen. He said to it: Write. It said: O Lord, what shall I write? He said: Write the destinies of everything until the Hour comes." Scholars differed over whether the pen, the created beings or the Throne was created first, on two views, mentioned by the memorizer Abu Ya'la al-Hamdani. The more correct of them is that the Throne came before the pen, because it is established in the Sahih, from the hadith of Abdullah ibn Umar, who said: The Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) said: "God decreed the destinies of creatures fifty thousand years before He created the heavens and the earth, His Throne being upon the water." This is explicit that the decreeing took place before the creation of the Throne, and the decreeing took place at the first creation of the pen, according to this hadith of Ubada. The saying "The first thing God created was the pen" and the rest is either one sentence or two. If it is one sentence, which is the sound view, its meaning is that at the first moment of its creation He said to it "Write", as in the wording "The first thing God created was the pen; He said to it: Write", with "first" and "the pen" in the accusative. If it is two sentences, as is also transmitted with "first" and "the pen" in the nominative, then it must be understood to mean the first of the created things of this world, so that the two hadiths agree. For the hadith of Abdullah ibn Umar explicitly states that the Throne preceded the decree, and the decree coincided with the creation of the pen. In another wording: "When God created the pen, He said to it: Write."

So this pen is the first of pens, the most excellent and most honoured. Many people of tafsir have said it is the pen by which God swore.

(Section)
The second pen is the pen of revelation, with which God's revelation is written to His prophets and messengers. The possessors of this pen are the rulers over the world, and the world serves them, and to them belong binding and loosing. All other pens serve their pens. On the night of the Night Journey the Prophet was raised to a level where he heard the scratching of pens. These are the pens that write what God, blessed and exalted, reveals of the matters by which the upper and lower world is governed.

(Section)
The third pen is the pen of signing on behalf of God and His Messenger. It is the pen of jurists and muftis. This pen too is a ruler, not ruled over, and to it disputes are referred concerning blood, property, private parts and rights. Its possessors inform about God's judgment which He passed among His servants. Its possessors are judges and kings over the owners of pens, and the pens of the world serve this pen.

(Section)
The fourth pen is the pen of the medicine of bodies, by which their existing health is preserved, their lost health is restored, and by which their afflictions and the conditions opposed to their health are repelled. After the pen of the medicine of religions, this is the most beneficial of pens, and people's need for its people is necessarily joined.

(Section)
The fifth pen is the signing on behalf of kings and their deputies, and the administration of the kingdom. For this reason its possessors are the most honoured of the possessors of pens and share with kings in governing states. If their pens are sound, the kingdom is sound; if their pens are corrupt, the kingdom is corrupt. They are intermediaries between kings and their subjects.

(Section)
The sixth pen is the pen of calculation, by which property is controlled: its income, its expenditure and its amounts. It is the pen of provisions, the pen of discrete and continuous quantity, by which amounts and the differences and proportions between them are controlled. Its basis is truthfulness and justice. If this pen lies and wrongs, the affairs of the kingdom are corrupted.

(Section)
The seventh pen is the pen of judgment, by which rights are established, cases are carried out, blood is shed, and property and rights are taken from the hand of the aggressor and returned to the rightful hand, by which a person is confirmed, and by which disputes end. Between this pen and the pen of signing on behalf of God there is general and specific relation: this one has enforceability and obligation, while that one has generality and comprehensiveness. This is a pen that stands on truthfulness in what it establishes and on justice in what it executes and carries out.

(Section)
The eighth pen is the pen of testimony, by which rights are preserved and protected from being lost, which stands between the wicked man and his denial, which confirms the truthful and refutes the liar, and which testifies for the rightful party to his right and against the false party to his falsehood. It is the trustee over blood, private parts, property, lineages and rights. When this pen betrays, the world is corrupted in the greatest corruption, and by its uprightness the affairs of the world are upright. Its basis is knowledge and not concealing.

(Section)
The ninth pen is the pen of interpretation. It is the scribe of the dream-vision, its explanation, its interpretation and what it is meant to convey. It is a noble, majestic pen that translates and reveals dream-revelation. It is among the pens suitable for both this world and religion. It depends on the purity, integrity and trustworthiness of its possessor, his pursuit of truth, good conduct and right methods, together with firm knowledge, inner clarity, a sense supported by divine light, and knowledge of the conditions, states and ways of people. It is one of the subtlest pens, the most far-ranging in its movement, the most extensive in its scope, and the most firmly attached to all existing things, the high and the low, and to past, present and future. Its operation within dreams is the place of its authority and the seat of its kingdom and sovereignty.

(Section)
The tenth pen is the pen of the world's histories and events. It is the pen by which occurrences are recorded and transmitted from one nation to another and from one generation to another. It gathers what has passed of the world and its events in the imagination and imprints it on the soul, so that the hearer seems to see and witness it. It is the pen of spiritual return, and this is the pen of wonders, for it restores the world to you in the form of imagination, so you see it with your heart and witness it with your insight.

(Section)
The eleventh pen is the pen of language and its details: explaining the meanings of its words, its grammar, its morphology, the secrets of its constructions, and what follows from these conditions, its aspects, the kinds of its signification, and how signification works. It is the pen of expressing meanings by choosing the finest, sweetest, easiest and clearest words. This pen has very wide scope, according to the breadth of words and the abundance and variety of their usages.

(Section)
The twelfth pen is the comprehensive pen. It is the pen of refuting the falsifiers, raising the sunnah of the upright, and exposing the falsehoods of the falsifiers in their various kinds and types, and clarifying their contradictions and incoherence, and their departure from truth and entry into falsehood. Among the pens this pen is like kings among people. Its possessors are people of proof, supporters of what the messengers brought, fighters against their enemies, and callers to God with wisdom and fair preaching, disputing with those who have strayed from His path by every kind of argument. The possessors of this pen are at war with every falsifier and enemy of every opponent of the messengers. They are engaged in one affair, while the other possessors of pens are engaged in another. These are the pens in which the order of the world's interests lies. It suffices for the nobility of the pen that God's books were written only by it, that God swore by it in His book, that He made Himself known to others through His having taught by the pen, and that what our Prophet was sent with reached us only through the medium of the pen. Abu Tammam composed beautifully when describing it:

You possess the supreme pen, whose point
Strikes the decisive matters and the joints,
Its spittle is a light dew, yet its fall
Brings, through its traces, East and West a torrent.
Its saliva is the poison of venomous snakes, its honey
The fruits of hands that gather honeycomb.
It has secret conferences which, were they not
Held in its company, the royal councils would not assemble.
Eloquent when you make it speak while it rides,
Dumb if you address it while it walks on foot.
When it mounts the subtle five fingers and the thoughts pour
Over it, the valleys of reflection being full,
The spear-points obey it, and the armies collapse
At its secret talk as tents collapse.
When the keen mind seeks to draw it out, and its high parts
Come down upon the paper, its low parts,
The two side-fingers aid it, and the three fingertips
Close its three sides.
You see a matter whose greatness is evident, though it is slender,
And whose speech is abundant, though its frame is lean.

(Section)
The matter sworn to by the pen and writing in this surah is the purification of His Prophet and Messenger from what his enemies say about him, namely His saying: ﴿You are not, by the favour of your Lord, a madman﴾.

If you match this oath with the thing sworn by, you will find that it points to it most clearly and plainly. For what the writer inscribes with the pen of the various sciences that humans transmit from one to another does not proceed from a madman, and proceeds only from complete intellect. How then could what the Messenger brought of this Book, which stands at the highest level of knowledge, come forth from a madman? Indeed, the sciences it contains are beyond human powers to produce, especially from an unlettered man who neither reads a book nor writes with his right hand, while it is at the highest level of eloquence, free from inconsistency and clear of contradiction. All the intelligent people, if they gathered in one place, would be unable to produce its like, even if they had the intellect of one man. How then could this come from a madman who has no intellect by which to distinguish what even many animals can distinguish? Is this not among the foulest slander and the clearest falsehood?

Reflect, then, on the testimony of this sworn-by thing to the sworn-about matter, and its indication of it in the fullest way. If a man composed a single excellent letter, orderly from beginning to end, its parts equal, each part confirming the others, or composed a poem of the same kind, or wrote a book of the same kind, intelligent people would testify to his intellect, and no one would dare to accuse him of madness, even though it is possible, indeed it has happened, that people have opposed it, matched it, or produced its like or something better. How then can one be accused of madness who brought what all intelligent people together were unable to oppose or equal, and who made known to them truth that their minds could not reach, so that the intellects of the intelligent submitted to it and the hearts of the saints bowed to it, and they were dissolved beside what he brought, so that they had no choice but to submit, obey and yield willingly, while seeing their own intellects as more needy and in greater want of what he brought, and with no perfection for them except through what he brought? He is the one who perfected their intellects, just as a child is perfected by nursing at the breast. For this reason his followers are the most intelligent of creatures in absolute terms. Their writings and books in the various fields, if you weigh them against the writings of his opponents, will show you the difference between them. It suffices for their intellects that they populated the world with knowledge and justice, and hearts with faith and piety. How then could their master be mad, when this is the state of his Book, his guidance and his conduct, and the state of his followers? All this was achieved for him and for them only by the grace of God upon him and upon them. Thus He negated madness from him by His blessing upon him.

Some scholars held that the bāʾ in ﴿bi-niʿmati rabbika﴾ is the bāʾ of oath, making it a separate oath interposed between the predicate and what it governs, as one says "mā anta bi-Llāhi bi-kādhib" (you are not a liar by God). This interpretation is very weak, because the first oath has already occurred, so how would a second oath come within its answer? It is not good to say "wa-Llāhi mā anta bi-Llāhi bi-qāʾim," and this is not eloquent speech nor known in their usage.

Another group held that the governing element of ﴿bi-niʿmati rabbika﴾ is the particle carrying the meaning of negation, or the meaning "I negate from you madness by the grace of your Lord." Abū ʿAmr Ibn al-Ḥājib and others rejected this view on the ground that particles do not govern by their meanings, but only by their wording.

Al-Zamakhsharī said: ﴿bi-niʿmati rabbika﴾ is connected to ﴿majnūn﴾ in its negated form, just as it is connected to ʿāqil in its affirmed form, as in your saying "anta bi-niʿmati Llāhi ʿāqil" (you are, by the grace of God, sound of mind). Affirmation and negation are equal in this, just as in your saying "ḍaraba Zaydun ʿAmran" and "mā ḍaraba Zaydun ʿAmran" — the verb governs in both affirmative and negative form with one and the same government. Its position is in the accusative as a circumstantial clause (ḥāl), meaning: "You are not mad, being favoured with that by your Lord." The bāʾ did not prevent majnūn from governing what precedes it, because it is a redundant particle serving to emphasize the negation.

This objection was raised against him: when the governing element falls upon a predicate that has a complement, two possibilities arise. The first is negating only that complement, as in your saying "mā Zaydun bi-dhāhibin musriʿan" (Zayd is not going quickly): the quickness is negated, but not the going itself, and there is no impediment to affirming going in a manner other than quickly. The second is negating the predicate itself, so that its complement is negated along with it: going is negated in this state, and quickness is negated with it. Thus if ﴿bi-niʿmati rabbika﴾ is made a complement of ﴿majnūn﴾, one of two things follows, and both are certainly false.

This objection here is faulty, because the meaning, once established as "you are not mad, being favoured by your Lord," entails with certainty the negation of madness when this report is true, and it is not valid to negate the complement while affirming the governing element in this statement. No one endowed with the faculty of understanding grasps from it anything other than this: madness has been removed from you by God's grace upon you, and the removal from us is what this objector understood: by God's grace upon us.

Then He, glorified, informed of the perfection of His Prophet's state in both his worldly life and the Hereafter, saying: ﴿And indeed for you is a reward never cut off.﴾ That is, uninterrupted, rather continuous and enduring. The word "reward" (ajr) is indefinite for the sake of magnification, as in His saying ﴿Indeed in that is a lesson﴾, ﴿Indeed in that is a sign﴾, ﴿Indeed in that is a reminder﴾, ﴿Indeed for the righteous is an achievement﴾, and ﴿And indeed for him with Us is nearness and a good return﴾, and it is frequent. The indefiniteness is for magnification because it presents to the hearer a matter of great magnitude that description cannot grasp and expression cannot attain.

Then He, glorified, informed of the perfection of His Prophet's state in both his worldly life and the Hereafter, saying: ﴿And indeed for you is a reward never cut off.﴾ That is, uninterrupted, rather continuous and enduring. Thus His signs in teaching speech are like His signs in the creation of man. Had it not been for the wonders of God's creation, these virtues would not have been established in flesh or sinew. Then God inspires man to join some of these together, and they become words standing by themselves. Then He inspires them to compose these words together, and they become speech indicating various meanings: command, prohibition, report, question, negation, affirmation, acknowledgment, denial, confirmation, denial, obligation, recommendation, asking and answering, and other kinds of address, in verse and prose, brief and extended, across the differences of the languages of creatures. They indicate His perfect power, His perfect knowledge, His perfect wisdom, His care for His creation, His gentleness and His beneficence.
