Commentary of Ibn al-Qayyim (al-Tafsir al-Qayyim) on surah 68, verse 42–43:

As for the place of gathering on the Day of Resurrection, the Exalted said: ﴿On the Day when the shin will be uncovered and they will be called to prostration, but they will not be able﴾

This is explicit that Allah calls all creatures to prostration on the Day of Resurrection, and that the disbelievers will be prevented from prostrating at that time. This obligation, which is beyond their capacity at that time, is a punishment for them in a sensory sense, because they were obligated to it in this world while they were able to do it. When they refrained from it while it was within their power, they were obligated to it when they could not do it, as a regret for them and a punishment for them. For this reason the Exalted said: ﴿And they used to be called to prostration while they were sound﴾ [al-Qalam: 43].

That is, their companions had no one preventing them from it. So when they abandoned it while they were sound, they were called to it at a time when they were prevented from it, as in the Sahih from the hadith of Zayd ibn Aslam, from ʿAṭāʾ, from Abu Saʿid (may Allah be pleased with him):

"Some people said: O Messenger of Allah, will we see our Lord?" — and he mentioned the hadith at length, until he said — "Then He will say: Let every community follow what it used to worship. The believers will say: We parted from the people in this world when we were most in need of them, and we did not keep their company.

He will say: I am your Lord. They will say: We seek refuge in Allah from You; we do not associate anything with Allah — two or three times — until some of them nearly turn back. Then He will say: Is there between you and Him a sign by which you recognise Him?"

They will say: Yes. Then the shin will be uncovered, and no one who used to prostrate of his own accord will remain except that Allah permits him to prostrate, and no one who used to prostrate for show and reputation will remain except that Allah makes his back one solid piece, so that whenever he wishes to prostrate he falls on his back. Then they will raise their heads."

And he mentioned the hadith.

This obligation is similar to the obligation of being questioned in the barzakh. Whoever answered willingly and by choice in this world will answer in the barzakh, and whoever refrained from answering in this world will be prevented from it in the barzakh. Obligating him in a state in which he is unable, while he has been prevented from the act, is not ugly; rather it is what the divine wisdom requires, because he was obligated at a time of ability and refused, so when he is obligated at a time of incapacity and has been prevented from the act, it is a punishment for him and a regret.

The point is that obligation does not cease until after entry into Paradise or Hell. It has already been mentioned that the hadith of al-Aswad ibn Sariʿ is sahih, and in it is the obligation in the place of gathering on the Day of Resurrection. So it agrees with the clear sound texts we have mentioned.

He said in (Ijtimaʿ al-Juyush al-Islamiyyah):

Reflect on what Muslim narrated in his Sahih from the hadith of Jabir ibn ʿAbd Allah (may Allah be pleased with them both).

When he was asked about the crossing over (al-wurud), he said: («We will come on the Day of Resurrection "upon a hill" above the people." He said: Then the nations will be called with their idols, and what they used to worship, the first after the first. Then our Lord, blessed and exalted, will come to us after that and say: Whom are you waiting for? They will say: We are waiting for our Lord. He will say: I am your Lord. They will say: Until we see You. Then He will manifest Himself to them, laughing. He said: Then He will set off with them and they will follow Him, and each person among them, whether hypocrite or believer, will be given a light. Then they will follow Him, and on the Bridge of Hell there are hooks and thorns that seize whom Allah the Exalted wills. Then the light of the hypocrites will be extinguished, and then the believers will be saved.

The first group will be saved, their faces like the full moon, seventy thousand of them, who will not be called to account. Then those who follow them, like the lights of a star in the sky, and so on. Then intercession will be granted and they will intercede, until whoever said "There is no god but Allah" and had in his heart good weighing a barley-grain will come out of the Fire. They will be placed at the courtyard of Paradise, and the people of Paradise will sprinkle water upon them.») And he mentioned the rest of the hadith.

Reflect on his words: «He sets off and they follow Him, and each person among them is given a light, the hypocrite and the believer», then reflect on the words of the Exalted: ﴿Allah took away their light and left them in darkness, they cannot see﴾ [al-Baqarah: 17], and the verse.

And reflect on their condition when their lights are extinguished, and they remain in darkness, while the believers go in the light of their faith following their Lord, Mighty and Majestic. And reflect on his words ﷺ in the hadith of intercession: «Let every community follow what it used to worship»; so every polytheist follows his god whom he used to worship. The monotheist is worthy of following the true God, besides whom every object of worship is false. And reflect on the words of the Exalted: ﴿On the Day when the shin will be uncovered and they will be called to prostration, but they will not be able﴾ [al-Qalam: 42]; he mentioned this verse in the hadith of intercession at this point, and his words in the hadith: "then His shin is uncovered", and this idafah (attribution) clarifies the meaning of the shin mentioned in the verse.

And reflect on the mention of setting off and His being followed, Glory be to Him, after this and that. It opens for you a door of the secrets of tawhid, the understanding of the Qur'an, and the way Allah the Glorified and Exalted treats the people of His tawhid, who worshipped Him alone and did not associate anything with Him. This is the treatment by which He dealt with the people of shirk in return: each community went with its object of worship, He set off with them, and they followed Him into the Fire. And the true God set off and His friends and worshippers followed Him. Glory be to Allah, Lord of the worlds, by whom the eyes of the people of tawhid are gladdened in this world and the Hereafter, and who parted from the people in it when they were most in need of them.

He said in (Ijtimaʿ al-Juyush al-Islamiyyah):

Reflect on what Muslim narrated in his Sahih from the hadith of Jabir ibn ʿAbd Allah (may Allah be pleased with them both).

When he was asked about the crossing over (al-wurud), he said: («We will come on the Day of Resurrection "upon a hill" above the people." He said: Then the nations will be called with their idols, and what they used to worship, the first after the first. Then our Lord, blessed and exalted, will come to us after that and say: Whom are you waiting for? They will say: We are waiting for our Lord. He will say: I am your Lord. They will say: Until we see You. Then He will manifest Himself to them, laughing. He said: Then He will set off with them and they will follow Him, and each person among them, whether hypocrite or believer, will be given a light. Then they will follow Him, and on the Bridge of Hell there are hooks and thorns that seize whom Allah the Exalted wills. Then the light of the hypocrites will be extinguished, and then the believers will be saved.

The first group will be saved, their faces like the full moon, seventy thousand of them, who will not be called to account. Then those who follow them, like the lights of a star in the sky, and so on. Then intercession will be granted and they will intercede, until whoever said "There is no god but Allah" and had in his heart good weighing a barley-grain will come out of the Fire. They will be placed at the courtyard of Paradise, and the people of Paradise will sprinkle water upon them.») And he mentioned the rest of the hadith.

Reflect on his words: «He sets off and they follow Him, and each person among them is given a light, the hypocrite and the believer», then reflect on the words of the Exalted: ﴿Allah took away their light and left them in darkness, they cannot see﴾ [al-Baqarah: 17], and the verse.

And reflect on their condition when their lights are extinguished, and they remain in darkness, while the believers go in the light of their faith following their Lord, Mighty and Majestic. And reflect on his words ﷺ in the hadith of intercession: «Let every community follow what it used to worship»; so every polytheist follows his god whom he used to worship. The monotheist is worthy of following the true God, besides whom every object of worship is false. And reflect on the words of the Exalted: ﴿On the Day when the shin will be uncovered and they will be called to prostration, but they will not be able﴾ [al-Qalam: 42]; he mentioned this verse in the hadith of intercession at this point, and his words in the hadith: "then His shin is uncovered", and this idafah (attribution) clarifies the meaning of the shin mentioned in the verse.

And reflect on the mention of setting off and His being followed, Glory be to Him, after this and that. It opens for you a door of the secrets of tawhid, the understanding of the Qur'an, and the way Allah the Glorified and Exalted treats the people of His tawhid, who worshipped Him alone and did not associate anything with Him. This is the treatment by which He dealt with the people of shirk in return: each community went with its object of worship, He set off with them, and they followed Him into the Fire. And the true God set off and His friends and worshippers followed Him. Glory be to Allah, Lord of the worlds, by whom the eyes of the people of tawhid are gladdened in this world and the Hereafter, and who parted from the people in it when they were most in need of them.

Commentary of Ibn al-Qayyim (al-Tafsir al-Qayyim) on surah 68, verse 48:

Ibn ʿAbbas said: He (God) forbade him (the Prophet) to imitate the companion of the fish (Dhu'l-Nun, Jonah), since he did not show patience as the people of steadfast resolve (ulu'l-ʿazm) showed patience.

Here there is a useful question, which is: the governing element (al-ʿamil) of the adverbial phrase (al-zarf), namely His words "when he called" (idh nadā), cannot be what is prohibited, for the meaning would become: "do not be like him in his calling."

God, glorified is He, has praised him for this call, informing us that He rescued him by means of it. He said:

﴿And Dhu'l-Nun, when he went off in anger, thinking that We would not decree (any hardship) for him, then he called out in the darkness: "There is no god but You; glory be to You; indeed I have been among the wrongdoers." So We answered him and rescued him from the distress, and thus do We save the believers.﴾

In al-Tirmidhi and others, it is related from the Prophet (ﷺ) that he said: "The supplication of my brother Dhu'l-Nun, when he was called upon in the belly of the fish: no distressed person has ever supplicated with it except that God relieved him: 'There is no god but You, glory be to You, indeed I have been among the wrongdoers.'"

It is therefore not possible that he (the Prophet) be forbidden to imitate him in this supplication, which is the call with which he called upon his Lord.

Rather, he was forbidden to imitate him in the cause that led to this calling, namely his anger, which led to his being confined in the belly of the fish, and the severity of that upon him until he called upon his Lord while he was distressed (makzum).

Al-kazīm and al-kāẓim are one who is filled with rage and anger, or with grief and sorrow, and who suppresses it and does not let it out.

If it is said: "Given that, what is the governing element of the adverbial phrase?"

It is said: it is the sense of the verbal action contained in "companion of the fish" (ṣāḥib al-ḥūt).

If it is said: "The question still stands, for when a prohibited matter is restricted by a condition or a time, it falls within the timeframe of the prohibition. If the meaning is: 'Do not be like the companion of the fish in this state, or at this time,' then it is a prohibition of that state."

It is said: since his calling was caused by his being the companion of the fish, He forbade that he be likened to him in the state which led him to become the companion of the fish and compelled him to call out, namely weakness of resolve and lack of patience with the decree of God, the Exalted. God, the Exalted, did not say: "And do not be like the companion of the fish, when he went off in anger, so the fish swallowed him and he called out," but rather He folded the story and abbreviated it, referred it to its mention in another place, and was satisfied with its outcome and what it ended in.

If it is said: "What prevents you from replacing the adverbial phrase with the very act that is prohibited? That is, 'do not be like him in his calling while he was full of rage, grief and distress; rather let your calling be the calling of one content with what his Lord decreed for him, who received it with contentment, submission and an expansive breast, not the calling of one suppressing (anger).'"

It is said: this meaning, although it is correct, the prohibition was not directed at imitating him in the bare act. Rather, he was forbidden to imitate him in the state that moved him to go off in anger, until he was imprisoned in the belly of the fish.

This is indicated by His words: ﴿So be patient for the decree of your Lord﴾, then He said: ﴿and do not be like the companion of the fish﴾, meaning in the weakness of his patience with the decree of his Lord. The state He forbade is the opposite of the state He commanded.

If it is said: "What prevents you from concluding that He commanded patience with His cosmic, predestined decree which He decreed upon him, and (that) 'do not be like the companion of the fish' refers to his not being patient with it, but instead calling out while distressed by its removal? He did not endure it or remain calm under it."

It is said: What prevents this is that God, glorified is He, praised Jonah and other of His prophets for asking Him to remove the harm that afflicted them. He praised him for that in His words:

﴿And Dhu'l-Nun, when he went off in anger, thinking that We would not decree (any hardship) for him, then he called out in the darkness: "There is no god but You; glory be to You; indeed I have been among the wrongdoers." So We answered him and rescued him from the distress, and thus do We save the believers.﴾

How, then, would He forbid imitating him in that for which He praises him and commends him? Likewise He praised Job in His words: ﴿Harm has touched me, and You are the Most Merciful of the merciful﴾, and Jacob in His words: ﴿I only complain of my anguish and grief to God﴾, and Moses in His words: ﴿My Lord, I am truly in need of whatever good You send down to me﴾.

And the seal of His prophets and messengers complained to Him, saying: "O God, I complain to You of the weakness of my strength and the scarcity of my resources, etc."

Complaint to Him, glorified is He, does not contradict beautiful patience; rather, a servant's turning away from complaining to others altogether, and making complaint to Him alone, is itself patience.

God, the Exalted, tests His servant in order to hear his complaint, his humble supplication and his prayer.

God, glorified is He, has censured those who do not humble themselves before Him and do not submit to Him at the time of trial, as He, the Exalted, said: ﴿And We indeed seized them with punishment, yet they did not submit to their Lord, nor did they humble themselves﴾.

The servant is too weak to display stoicism before his Lord, and the Lord, the Exalted, did not desire that His servant display stoicism before Him; rather He desired from him that he be submissive to Him and humble himself before Him. He, the Exalted, abhors one who complains of Him to His creation, and loves one who complains to Him of what afflicts him.

It was said to one of them: "How do you complain to Him of what is not hidden from Him?"

He said: "My Lord is pleased by the humiliation of His servant before Him."

The point is: He, glorified is He, commanded His Messenger to be patient with the patience of the people of steadfast resolve, who were patient with His decree by choice.

This is the most perfect patience, and for this reason the story of intercession on the Day of Resurrection revolves around these (prophets), until they refer it to the best and most excellent of them, the most patient with the decree of God, may the blessings and peace of God be upon them all.

(A subtle point)

One of the knowers (ʿārifīn) had in his pocket a slip of paper which he would take out at all times and look at, and on it was written: ﴿So be patient for the decree of your Lord, for indeed you are before Our eyes.﴾

ʿUmar ibn al-Khattab, may God be pleased with him, said: "If patience and gratitude were two camels, I would not mind which of them I rode."

Muhammad ibn Shubrumah, whenever affliction befell him, would say: "A summer cloud, then it will clear away."

Commentary of Ibn al-Qayyim (al-Tafsir al-Qayyim) on surah 68, verse 51:

Many of the exegetes have said, regarding the words of the Most High: ﴿And indeed, the disbelievers would almost make you slip with their eyes when they hear the Reminder﴾, that it refers to affliction by the evil eye (al-ʿayn). They wanted to afflict the Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) with it, so a group of those who cast the evil eye looked at him, and they said, "We have never seen the like of him, nor the like of his proof." A group of them would pass by a she-camel or a fat cow, cast the evil eye upon it, and then say to their servant, "Take the basket and the dirham and bring us some of its meat." It would not be long before it fell and was slaughtered.

Al-Kalbi said: "A man among the Arabs would remain for two or three days without eating, then he would lift the side of his tent, and the camels would pass by him. He would say, 'I have never seen camels or sheep better than these today.' Not long would pass before a group of them fell. The disbelievers asked this man to afflict the Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) with the evil eye and to do to him what he had done to others. But Allah the Exalted protected His Messenger, guarded him, and revealed to him: ﴿And indeed, the disbelievers would almost make you slip with their eyes﴾."

This is the view of one group. Another group, including Ibn Qutaybah, said: "The intended meaning is not that they afflict you with the evil eye as the one who casts the evil eye afflicts with his eye that which pleases him. Rather, it means that they look at you when you recite the Noble Qur'an with a very intense look born of enmity and hatred, a look that would almost cast you down." Al-Zajjaj said: "That is, from the intensity of their enmity, they would with their looks, the look of hatred, almost throw you down." This usage is common in speech; the speaker says, "He looked at me with a look that almost knocked me down." He said: "The soundness of this meaning is confirmed by the fact that He linked this look with the hearing of the Noble Qur'an, and they were extremely averse to that, so they directed at him a look of hatred, a look that has an effect on the one looked at."

I say: The look that affects the one looked at may arise from the intensity of enmity and envy, so that his look affects me just as his soul is affected by envy, and the influence of the soul is strengthened at the moment of confrontation. For when an enemy is absent from his enemy, he may occupy his soul with other things; but when he sees him face to face, his resolve gathers upon him and his soul turns entirely toward him, so he is affected by his look, to the extent that some people fall, some fever, and some are carried home.

People have witnessed much of this.

It may also arise from admiration, which is what they call affliction by the evil eye: the one who looks sees a thing with an admiring or awe-struck look, so his spirit takes on a particular quality that affects the one looked at. This is what people know of the glance of the one who casts the evil eye: they admire a thing and marvel at it, and so the one they admire is afflicted.

ʿAbd al-Razzaq ibn Maʿmar related from Hisham ibn Qutaybah, who said: "This is what Abu Hurayrah related to us, who said: The Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) said:

"The evil eye is real." Related by al-Bukhari and Muslim.

"And he forbade tattooing." Related by al-Bukhari and Muslim.

Sufyan related from ʿAmr ibn Dinar, from ʿUrwah, from ʿAmir, from ʿUbayd ibn Rifaʿah, that Asma' bint ʿUmays said: "O Messenger of Allah (ﷺ), the sons of my son Jaʿfar are afflicted by the evil eye; may I seek a cure (ruqyah) for them?" He said: "Yes. For if anything could overtake the decree, the evil eye would overtake it."

(Authentic).

So the disbelievers were looking at him with the look of a fiercely hostile envier, a look that would almost have made him slip, were it not for Allah's protection and safeguarding. This is more severe than the look of the one who casts the evil eye; indeed it is a kind of it. Whoever says it is affliction by the evil eye means this meaning, and whoever says it is not means that their look was not a look of approval and admiration. And the Noble Qur'an is true.

Al-Tirmidhi related from the hadith of Abu Saʿid: "That the Prophet (ﷺ) used to seek refuge from the evil eye of a human being."

(Authentic).

Had the evil eye not been an evil, he would not have sought refuge from it. In al-Tirmidhi, from the hadith of ʿAli ibn al-Mubarak, from Yahya ibn Abi Kathir, who said: Ḥābis ibn Ḥabbah al-Tamimi related to me, my father related to me, that he heard the Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) say: "There is no contagion (hamah), and the evil eye is real."

(Weak), but his saying "the evil eye is real" is authentic.

Also in it, from the hadith of Wuhayb, from Ibn Tawus, from his father, from Ibn ʿAbbas, who said: "The Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) used to say: If anything could overtake the decree, the evil eye would overtake it. And when you are asked to wash (for the one who is afflicted), then wash."

Related by Muslim.
